Counsel for Respondent :- Abhijeet Ghosh,Ashish Kumar,G.A.,Gaurav Sharma Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1. Heard Sri P.K. Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Ashish Kumar, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. appearing for the State -respondents.

2. The present writ petition has been filed praying to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 14.02.2024, registered as Case Crime No.0096 of 2024, under Sections 376, 377, 420, 406,
313, 506, 120-B I.P.C. and Section 67-A of Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station Sadar Bazar, District Agra.

sentences.text: Initially the matter was referred to Mediation Centre vide order dated 22.03.2024, however, as per mediation report the same has failed.
Thereafter, both the parties settled their dispute outside the Court and therefore, vide order dated 04.09.2024, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre.

4. Perused the settlement agreement dated 08.09.2024 which indicates that matter has been peacefully settled between the parties and they have settled their differences on the terms mentioned in paragraph 6 of the settlement agreement dated 08.09.2024.

The paragraph no.6 is quoted as under:-
"6. The following settlement has been arrived at between the Parties hereto:-
a) That the parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the court and the petitioner Yogendra Singh has already paid Rs.15,00,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Lakh only) to the Respondent No.3-Aakanksha which has been duly acknowledged by the Respondent No.3-Aakanksha, as such there remains no dispute between the parties.

b) That the parties have already settled their dispute and now they do not want to litigate further, as such the cases filed by them against each other regarding present dispute shall be withdrawn by the parties concerned by taking appropriate steps before the Court/authority concerned.
c) That the parties will not file any fresh case against each other in respect of this dispute.
They have no claim against each other in future also."
5. It is submitted that as between the parties compromise had already taken place therefore, the impugned First Information Report is liable to be quashed.

6. The submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner have already been noted in paragraph nos.3 and 4 of the order dated 22.03.2024 and therefore, no offence as alleged under Section 376, 377 I.P.C. is made out.

7. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2003(4) SCC 675 (B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana), J.T. 2008(9) SC 192 (Nikhil Merchant Vs.
Central Bureau of investigation and another), (2012) 10 SCC 303 (Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab),
(2014) 9 SCC 653 (Yogendra Yadav and others Vs. State of Jharkhand) and also (2014) 6 SCC 466 (Narendra Singh Vs. State of Punjab), and in view of the settlement agreement dated 08.09.2024 the First Information Report dated 14.02.2024, registered as Case Crime No.0096 of 2024, under Sections 376, 377, 420, 406, 313, 506, 120-B I.P.C. and Section 67-A of Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station Sadar Bazar, District Agra is hereby quashed.
